title: ElevenLabs Voice Cloning for Creators: How to Create a Reusable AI Voice
markdown:
ElevenLabs Voice Cloning is worth evaluating if you want to turn text into speech in a version of your own voice for work such as podcast updates, video voiceovers, or audiobook narration. ElevenLabs describes the workflow as uploading or recording an audio sample, letting its system analyze the voice, then generating speech from text. [Source: ElevenLabs Voice Cloning](https://elevenlabs.io/voice-cloning)

## Start with the cloning mode

Choose **Instant Voice Cloning** when your priority is a quicker test or a personal content workflow. ElevenLabs says this mode can use 1–5 minutes of audio, creates a replica in seconds, supports 32+ languages automatically, and provides controls including pitch and speaking pace. [Source: ElevenLabs Voice Cloning](https://elevenlabs.io/voice-cloning)

Choose **Professional Voice Cloning** when you can provide more source material and want the provider’s highest-quality option. ElevenLabs says Professional Voice Cloning requires 30+ minutes of clean audio and is intended to capture subtle intonation and emotion; its pricing page lists the feature with the Creator plan. [Voice Cloning details](https://elevenlabs.io/voice-cloning) [Pricing details](https://elevenlabs.io/pricing)

## Check the plan before paying

The official pricing page lists a Free plan with 10,000 monthly credits, Starter at $6 per month with Instant Voice Cloning, and Creator at $22 per month with Professional Voice Cloning; it also states that prices exclude taxes, levies, and duties. Credits are shared across products, so assess the rest of your anticipated usage before selecting a plan. [ElevenLabs pricing](https://elevenlabs.io/pricing)

Use only audio you are authorized to clone. ElevenLabs states that voice cloning is possible only with the voice owner’s explicit permission and describes safeguards intended to help prevent misuse. [Responsible-use information](https://elevenlabs.io/voice-cloning)
